prompt:
Take the first reference photograph and change ONE thing in it: the markings
painted on the road.

Everything else stays exactly as it is: the same Berlin corner from the same
camera position, the same wide vertical framing, the same young man in the
navy blue polo shirt and beige chinos standing with his back to us on the
grey cobbles behind the granite kerb, the same cyclist in the bright yellow
jacket and dark grey helmet entering at the bottom edge of the picture on
his dark grey bicycle, exactly where he already is and exactly the size he
already is, the same pedestrian traffic light with the upper round lens
glowing an even plain red, the same facade, the same flat overcast daylight.

THE ONE CHANGE is on the road in front of the waiting man. Starting at the
kerb where he waits and running across the road away from the camera, a
pedestrian crossing of broad white bars is painted on the grey asphalt, the
same bars as in the second reference photograph. The red bicycle strip runs
beside it on the RIGHT, its dashed white edge between the two, so the
crossing reads as two lanes side by side: the white bars in front of the
waiting man, the red strip to their right, and the cyclist out on the red
strip.
